reference: Bash metadata and the builtin's documented help are contracts. Signature listing is compared with util-linux wipefs under system Bash: images are built by util-linux mkswap, e2fsprogs mkfs.ext2 and a Python writer called by absolute path, so both sides list the same bytes, and the table and parsable formats are compared exactly.
coverage: Bash reports wipefs as a builtin with the executable search path disabled by the runner.
Bash help registration and the loadable's published synopsis are checked.
The command's own --help output is checked against its published help text.
Future safe inspection, dry-run, and erase behavior is specified as deferred work with independent reference requirements.
Read-only listing and -n/--no-act on independently encoded private regular files; missing operands and aggregate continuation.
exclusions: Raw devices and actual -a erasure remain deferred to a disposable VM or reviewed pwrite mock.
The concise offset/type/path rows are a custom contract, not full util-linux probing parity.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash resolves the loadable as a builtin when candidate execution uses an empty PATH.
Verify Bash has registered help for wipefs; the marker makes the expected output independent of help formatting.
Check Bash's short-help form against the usage synopsis declared in the builtin table entry.
Check wipefs --help prints the builtin's documented modes, options and signature-family scope without opening a target.
cases.stdout:
List or erase filesystem, swap and partition-table signatures.

    wipefs device          table of detected signatures
    wipefs -a device       erase every detected signature
    wipefs -o OFF device   erase the signature at offset OFF
    -n  write nothing      -q  no erase messages    -f  erase a device in use
    -i  no table heading   -p  parsable listing

Recognises vfat, swap, xfs, ext2/3/4, iso9660, ntfs, btrfs, dos and gpt.

cases.purpose: List a swap signature made by util-linux mkswap with its UUID and label in default, -n and --no-act modes, byte-identical to util-linux wipefs, and confirm the image is unchanged.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import sys; open(sys.argv[1], "wb").write(bytes(1048576))' image
/usr/bin/chmod 600 image
/usr/sbin/mkswap -U 33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333 -L charlie image >/dev/null
/usr/bin/cp image image.orig
wipefs image
wipefs -n image
wipefs --no-act image
/usr/bin/cmp image image.orig && echo unchanged

cases.purpose: Qualify -a byte changes, including multiple signatures and preservation of unrelated fixture data.
Empty and unmatched private regular files are silent and unchanged in both independent util-linux and candidate runs.
cases.script:
: > empty
printf 'ordinary bytes\n' > plain
wipefs empty plain

cases.purpose: List two signatures at their offsets in one image (an e2fsprogs ext2 superblock at 0x438 and a DOS partition table at 0x1fe), as a table and with -n -i -p, byte-identical to util-linux wipefs, and confirm the image is unchanged. The images are removed at the end because mkfs.ext2 stamps a creation time and hash seed into them.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import sys; open(sys.argv[1], "wb").write(bytes(1048576))' image
/usr/sbin/mkfs.ext2 -q -F -U 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111 -L alpha image
/usr/bin/python3 -c '
import struct, sys
with open(sys.argv[1], "r+b") as f:
    f.seek(0x1b8); f.write(struct.pack("<I", 0x12345678))
    f.seek(0x1be); f.write(bytes([0, 0, 2, 0, 0x83, 0, 0, 0]) + struct.pack("<II", 1, 2047))
    f.seek(0x1fe); f.write(b"\x55\xaa")' image
/usr/bin/cp image image.orig
wipefs image
wipefs -n -i -p image
/usr/bin/cmp image image.orig && echo unchanged
/usr/bin/rm -f image image.orig

cases.purpose: A missing operand fails with status 1 and a diagnostic, and wipefs stops there without listing the later image, as util-linux wipefs does. The images are removed at the end because mkfs.ext2 stamps a creation time and hash seed into them.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import sys; open(sys.argv[1], "wb").write(bytes(1048576))' image
/usr/sbin/mkfs.ext2 -q -F -U 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111 -L alpha image
rc=0
wipefs absent image || rc=$?
/usr/bin/rm -f image
exit "$rc"
